finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl: the user-supplied `f` parameter is joined to /srv/files with filepath.Join, which cleans `..` segments but does not confine the result to the root. An unauthenticated attacker can read any file the process can access.
finding.source: HTTP query parameter `f` on GET /dl (r.URL.Query().Get("f"), files.go:12), served publicly on :8082 with no authentication
finding.sink: os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)) at files.go:13, with the file contents written to the response at files.go:18

trace.note: /dl is registered to download on the default mux, which has no auth middleware
http.ListenAndServe(":8082") binds all interfaces, so the endpoint is public
name is taken from the `f` query parameter without validation
filepath.Join("/srv/files", "../../etc/passwd") cleans to /etc/passwd, which escapes the root
the file bytes are returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No filepath.Base, no prefix check against root after Join, no filepath.IsLocal or os.Root use, and no authentication or authorization middleware. The only error handling is the 404 on read failure, which is not a security control. By contrast, avatar() at files.go:22 applies filepath.Base and is not vulnerable, so I did not report it. Reproduction: curl 'http://host:8082/dl?f=../../etc/passwd'

verdict.reason: files.go:12-13 passes the unvalidated `f` query value to filepath.Join(root, name), which collapses `..` and escapes /srv/files, and files.go:32/34 expose /dl on :8082 with no auth, so the file bytes are written back at files.go:18.
